setup: A child care center staff member is signed in from a standard web browser on a tablet or desktop computer, and the organization uses Nenios as its online management portal.
action: The staff member opens the Nenios application from the browser.
expected_observation: The system loads as a web-based child care management portal in the browser without requiring a local desktop application.

setup: The child care center has active records for families, children, enrollments, billing, and staff schedules in Nenios.
action: An administrator views the main dashboard and navigates to the family, enrollment, billing, and child information areas.
expected_observation: The system provides access to day-to-day administration functions, staff workflow screens, and centralized records for families, enrollment, billing, and child information.

setup: An administrator, an office staff member, a teacher, and a parent or guardian each have valid access roles in Nenios.
action: Each stakeholder signs in and opens the areas of the system intended for their role.
expected_observation: The system presents role-appropriate outputs and access for administrators, office staff, teachers, and parents or guardians according to their user permissions.

setup: A staff member is signed in with permission to manage family records, and no existing family profile is open.
action: The staff member creates a new family profile, enters parent or guardian contact details, and links one or more children to the family.
expected_observation: The family profile is saved with the entered contact details and the linked child records are visible on the family profile.

setup: The enrollment list contains a mix of currently enrolled children, pending children, and children on a waiting list with assigned positions.
action: A staff member opens the enrollment management screen.
expected_observation: The system displays which children are enrolled, which are pending, and each waiting-list child's position in line.

setup: A child is on the waiting list for a classroom, and an available spot has been created for that classroom.
action: A staff member selects the waiting-list child and confirms the move to active enrollment.
expected_observation: The child's status changes from waiting list to active enrollment and the enrollment record reflects the new status.

setup: A classroom or age-group roster has an opening, and multiple children are waiting for placement in that same classroom or age group.
action: A staff member opens the waiting-list placement view for the available classroom or age group.
expected_observation: The system identifies the next child in line for the appropriate classroom or age group and displays that child as the next candidate for placement.

setup: A child is selected for moving from the waiting list into a classroom that is already at or above its allowed capacity.
action: A staff member attempts to confirm the waiting-list-to-enrollment move.
expected_observation: The system checks classroom capacity first and blocks the move if no capacity is available, showing a clear capacity-related message instead of confirming enrollment.

setup: The center has multiple classrooms organized by age group, and each classroom has a defined maximum capacity with some spots filled and some open.
action: An office staff member opens the classroom capacity overview.
expected_observation: The system shows capacity tracking for each classroom and age group, including current occupancy and remaining available spots.

setup: A classroom has reached its maximum allowed child count based on the center's capacity rules.
action: A staff member tries to add another child to that classroom.
expected_observation: The system prevents the over-enrollment action and does not allow the classroom to exceed its permitted capacity.

setup: The center has several classrooms and age groups with varying numbers of open spots, and staff need a current availability snapshot.
action: A staff member opens the quick-view availability screen.
expected_observation: The system displays available classroom spots by classroom and age group in a concise view that can be reviewed quickly.

setup: A child profile is being created or edited by a staff member with permission to manage child records.
action: The staff member enters the child's health history and immunization details and saves the profile.
expected_observation: The system stores the child profile together with the health and immunization information and makes it retrievable from the child record.

setup: Some child records have complete and current health and immunization information, while others are missing one or more required items or are out of date.
action: A staff member opens the child records list or compliance view.
expected_observation: The system clearly indicates which child health and immunization records are current and which have missing information.

setup: The center maintains compliance tracking for child health and immunization documentation across enrolled children.
action: An administrator opens the compliance monitoring view for child health and immunization records.
expected_observation: The system presents compliance status for children, highlighting records that meet requirements and those that need follow-up.

setup: A family has one or more enrolled children, and the billing rules include applicable care schedules and fees for those enrollments.
action: The billing cycle is run or the system recalculates charges for the family.
expected_observation: The system generates charges for the family based on each child's enrollment and the applicable care schedule or fee structure.

setup: An authorized staff member is signed into Nenios Child Care Management and opens a child's account that already contains billed charges, posted payments, and a remaining balance.
action: The staff member views the account's billing summary for that child or family.
expected_observation: The system displays what has been billed, what has been paid, and the current outstanding amount in a clear, itemized view.

setup: A parent has requested a statement or receipt for childcare charges, and an authorized staff member is viewing the family's billing record.
action: The staff member selects the option to generate a statement or receipt for the parent.
expected_observation: The system produces a parent-ready statement or receipt that includes the relevant billing details and can be shared or printed.

setup: A parent is associated with a current enrollment record, billing record, and recent child or center update in the system.
action: An authorized staff member opens the parent information summary for that family.
expected_observation: The system presents clear parent-facing information covering enrollment status, billing status, and relevant child or center updates in a readable format.

setup: Staff need to send the same enrollment and billing information to multiple parents during a busy operations period.
action: An authorized staff member uses the central system to share a prepared parent-facing update instead of creating individual messages manually.
expected_observation: The system allows the staff member to distribute consistent information quickly from a shared source, reducing the need to draft separate manual communications.

setup: The center has active enrollments, some open vacancies, unpaid balances, and children with upcoming immunization concerns recorded in the system.
action: An authorized staff member opens the internal operational report dashboard.
expected_observation: The system shows operational reporting for enrollment counts, vacancies, outstanding balances, and upcoming immunization issues.

setup: The center is open for the day and attendance and classroom assignment data have been recorded for current children.
action: An authorized staff member opens the daily snapshot view.
expected_observation: The system displays a same-day snapshot of enrollment and classroom occupancy, showing current counts by classroom or group.

setup: The center has children on the waiting list and at least one available spot in an enrollment or classroom capacity record.
action: An authorized staff member opens the waiting list and open spots view.
expected_observation: The system displays the current waiting list alongside any open spots, allowing staff to see availability and pending demand in one place.

setup: The billing system contains one or more unpaid invoices for enrolled families.
action: An authorized staff member opens the billing summary report.
expected_observation: The system shows a billing summary that lists unpaid invoices, including the families or accounts they belong to and the amounts still due.

setup: Child health records contain immunizations that are due soon, overdue, or missing for one or more children.
action: An authorized staff member opens the health reminder view.
expected_observation: The system displays a reminder list of immunizations that are due or missing, grouped clearly enough for follow-up action.

setup: A staff member with appropriate permissions is logged into the central Nenios system and has updated child, enrollment, or billing information available.
action: The authorized staff member shares or publishes the updated information through the central system.
expected_observation: The system makes the latest approved information available through the central source so that other authorized staff can view the same current details.

setup: A family record exists with linked enrollment, billing, and child information stored in the Nenios system.
action: An authorized staff member searches for the family by name or child identifier and opens the record.
expected_observation: The system returns the family's stored information from central records, including family details, enrollment data, billing data, and child information in one lookup flow.

setup: Staff regularly need to prepare repeated parent communications and retrieve recurring operational details during the workday.
action: An authorized staff member completes a typical task such as reviewing a child account, generating a parent update, or checking a report using the central system.
expected_observation: The task can be completed with fewer manual steps than preparing the same information from separate paper or spreadsheet sources, reducing staff workload.

setup: A family has one current record in the system with active enrollment and billing information, and the same family's details are being viewed by staff.
action: An authorized staff member updates the family's information in the central record and then opens the related enrollment and billing views.
expected_observation: The system shows the family, enrollment, and billing information consistently from the same stored record, with updates reflected in one place rather than conflicting across multiple copies.

setup: A new or infrequent staff member is given access to the system during normal operating hours.
action: The staff member attempts a common task such as finding a child record, viewing billing status, or opening a daily report without formal assistance.
expected_observation: The staff member can complete the task with straightforward navigation and understandable labels, indicating the system is easy to learn quickly.

setup: The system is being used during routine daily center operations by multiple staff members handling enrollment, billing, and parent updates.
action: Staff perform normal lookups and reporting tasks across the day, including checking records and sharing updates.
expected_observation: The system remains usable and dependable for routine operations, with information accessible when needed and without introducing confusing or disruptive behavior.

setup: An employee is signed into the Nenios Child Care Management system with the Office Staff role, and the account is assigned only to front-desk and billing duties.
action: The employee opens a child record and attempts to access the staff payroll section and the classroom lesson planning area.
expected_observation: The system allows access only to Office Staff functions and hides or blocks payroll and teaching pages, showing an access denied message for sections outside the employee's job role.

setup: The system contains three active users: one Office Staff user, one Teacher user, and one Administrator user, each signed in with their own role.
action: Each user opens the main navigation and views the available menus and record-editing options.
expected_observation: The Office Staff user, Teacher user, and Administrator user see different sets of menus and permissions, confirming that their access levels are not identical.

setup: A teacher is signed into the system, and the child profile contains sensitive fields such as emergency contacts, custody notes, and medical alerts.
action: The teacher opens the child profile and tries to view and edit the sensitive fields.
expected_observation: Sensitive information is either hidden or read-only for the teacher, and the system prevents unauthorized changes; only authorized staff can view or update those fields.

setup: An administrator has access to audit logging, and an existing child attendance record is visible in the system.
action: The administrator edits the attendance record by changing the recorded pickup time and saves the update.
expected_observation: An audit entry is created showing the name of the person who made the change, the specific field changed, the old and new values, and the date and time of the update.

setup: Several audit trail entries already exist for record changes made by different staff members across multiple dates.
action: A manager opens the audit trail screen and searches for entries by staff name, date range, and record type.
expected_observation: The system returns matching audit entries in a usable list so the manager can review who made changes, when they occurred, and which records were affected.

setup: A dispute has been raised about a child's authorized pickup status, and audit trail entries exist for related edits and approvals.
action: An administrator opens the audit trail for the child's record and reviews the history of changes related to pickup authorization.
expected_observation: The system displays the sequence of audit entries clearly enough to review decisions, track corrections or errors, and answer questions about who changed the record and why during the dispute review.

setup: The parent portal is available, and a parent account is linked to one enrolled child.
action: The parent signs in and opens the child information and daily activity pages.
expected_observation: The system shows only the parent-facing information that has been defined for the release, while any staff-generated or internal-only details remain hidden; the visibility boundary is treated as configurable pending final confirmation.

setup: A waiting list contains children with different application dates and at least one sibling already enrolled.
action: A staff member reviews the waiting list ranking screen after entering a new application.
expected_observation: The system displays the waiting list order according to the current configured priority rules without assuming an unconfirmed policy, and any unresolved priority factors are not presented as fixed behavior.

setup: The system is being prepared for reporting and recordkeeping in an environment where compliance and licensing obligations have not yet been finalized.
action: A manager attempts to generate a standard operational report and inspects the available data fields and export options.
expected_observation: The report includes only the currently approved fields and clearly reflects the active compliance configuration, without exposing unconfirmed regulated data requirements or claiming support for missing licensing-specific outputs.

setup: A staff member is signed in on a device in a shared office environment, and the system contains personally identifiable child and family information.
action: The staff member opens a child record and leaves the screen unattended, then another unauthenticated person tries to return to the same record from the device.
expected_observation: Sensitive data is protected through the current security and privacy controls, such as session timeout, re-authentication, or restricted access, and the system does not leave private child or family information exposed to an unauthorized viewer.
